We bring curiosity, creativity, and technical skills, with an appreciation for last-minute breakthroughs

summary: PyroBridge is an interactive satellite fire observatory that helps people compare fire activity across the MODIS and VIIRS eras. Users can explore a global snapshot of more than 81,000 NASA FIRMS hotspot detections, zoom into six historical fire landscapes, and compare observed and estimated monthly counts in a downloadable calendar. We tested two ways to estimate what VIIRS might have reported from older MODIS records, using 648 region-months and withholding a full year at a time. The dashboard shows where the estimates improve on raw MODIS counts and where they fall short. This makes it easier to investigate seasonal patterns and unusual activity while keeping the original observations, model estimates, and uncertainty visible.
details:
PyroBridge combines a global hotspot globe, six regional investigations, and a monthly fire activity calendar. The global snapshot contains 74,304 NOAA-20 VIIRS detections and 7,031 Aqua MODIS detections. The historical investigations cover Evros, Evia, Rhodes, Manavgat, Gran Chaco, and Northern Pantanal. Users can inspect individual detections over dated NASA imagery, compare sensors, and export monthly counts and estimates as CSV.

We built a reproducible Python pipeline and a browser dashboard using TypeScript, React, Vite, and MapLibre GL JS. The pipeline tests seasonal scaling and LightGBM using MODIS counts, season, and location. We evaluated the monthly models on 648 overlapping region-months across 13 whole-year holdouts. In Evros, seasonal scaling reduced mean absolute error from 50.78 to 14.50 detections per month compared with using raw MODIS counts as the estimate. Performance varied by region, and the dashboard shows the original baseline alongside both models.

The interactive calibration lets users make a prediction and then reveal the withheld VIIRS reading. This helps students and analysts see how a change in sensor can affect the apparent fire record. We considered cloud cover, satellite overpass timing, sensor resolution, and missing observations. A separate matched-pass benchmark checks usable coverage. The monthly estimates remain experimental, with cloud cover and overpass effort unadjusted. A hotspot is a detected thermal pixel, and several pixels can belong to the same fire.
